articles.title: SFO Technologies And Cochin Shipyard Jointly Develops India's First Indigenous Hybrid ...
articles.content: India has taken a significant step forward in advanced manufacturing with the unveiling of the country’s first indigenously designed and manufactured Hybrid Laser Arc Welding (HLAW) technology, announced Cochin Shipyard. The breakthrough has been jointly developed by SFO Technologies Pvt. Ltd., the flagship company of NeST Group, and Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL). The announcement was made on 11 November 2026 during the inauguration of the Advanced Laser Engineering Centre and Hybrid Laser Arc Welding R&D Facility at NeST Hitek Park in Kalamassery, Kochi. The facility was inaugurated by Jose V. J., Chairman and Managing Director of CSL, and Dr N. Jehangir, Chairman and Managing Director of SFO Technologies. The newly developed HLAW system combines laser welding, conventional arc welding, robotics and advanced automation into a single integrated platform. A key feature of the system is its high-power fibre laser source, which has been indigenously developed by SFO Technologies, marking an important achievement in domestic industrial technology development. The technology is expected to deliver substantially faster welding speeds, deeper weld penetration, reduced material distortion and greater weld consistency. These advantages could improve productivity and manufacturing efficiency across a broad range of sectors, including shipbuilding, defence, heavy engineering, railways, energy and other strategic industries involved in the fabrication of large tanks, wagons and complex industrial structures. The development is particularly noteworthy for India’s shipbuilding sector, where welding represents a critical component of vessel construction. By enhancing manufacturing repeatability, structural quality and production efficiency, the system has the potential to strengthen the competitiveness of Indian shipyards and industrial manufacturers. The project also represents a major contribution to the country’s efforts to reduce dependence on imported laser welding platforms and establish stronger indigenous capabilities in advanced manufacturing technologies. It aligns closely with the broader objective of increasing technological self-reliance in strategically important industrial sectors. “This is a proud moment not only for SFO Technologies but for Indian manufacturing. By developing the high-power fiber laser source in-house and integrating it with advanced welding, robotics and automation, we have demonstrated that high-end manufacturing technologies can be conceived, engineered and built in India,” said Dr N. Jehangir. Highlighting the importance of the collaboration, Jose V. J. said that the partnership demonstrated how engineering innovation could be applied to address practical industrial requirements. “Cochin Shipyard’s collaboration with SFO Technologies has enabled the joint development of a technology that is relevant to shipbuilding and other manufacturing industries. The Indigenous Hybrid Laser Arc Welding has the potential to improve productivity, quality and competitiveness across Indian manufacturing,” he said. The Advanced Laser Engineering Centre will serve as a hub for research, testing, validation and commercialisation of advanced laser technologies. Beyond supporting industrial adoption, the facility is expected to contribute to the objectives of Atmanirbhar Bharat while helping position Kochi as an emerging centre for high-end industrial innovation and advanced manufacturing in India. The introduction of indigenous HLAW technology comes at a time when nations are increasingly seeking domestic control over critical manufacturing capabilities. articles.title: AIIMS-Delhi performs India's first open foetal surgery to repair severe spinal defect
articles.content: In a medical first for India, AIIMS, Delhi has successfully performed an open foetal surgery to repair a severe spinal defect in an unborn baby at 25 weeks’ gestation, aiming to prevent further damage to the developing spinal cord, the premier institute said on Saturday. The six-hour procedure, performed on November 12, involved repairing a lumbosacral myelomeningocele, the most severe form of spina bifida, while the foetus was still in the womb, it said. The surgery was performed after more than five weeks of multidisciplinary planning, detailed foetal imaging, counselling, anaesthetic preparation and operative simulation, the hospital said. The neurosurgical component was led by Dr Deepak Gupta, while the maternal-foetal medicine and obstetric teams were led by Dr Neena Malhotra and Dr K Aparna Sharma. More than 30 clinicians and nurses from obstetrics and gynaecology, maternal-foetal medicine, neurosurgery, obstetric and neuroanaesthesia, plastic surgery, radiodiagnosis and neonatology participated in the procedure. The multidisciplinary surgery was carried out at the Neurosciences Centre using high-end microscopy and continuous ultrasonography assistance. “This establishes an important new capability for fetal care and paediatric neurosurgery in India,” Dr Gupta, President of the Indian Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery, said. “In rigorously selected cases, prenatal repair seeks to limit ongoing injury to exposed neural tissue, reduce the subsequent need for cerebrospinal-fluid diversion for hydrocephalus, and improve selected neurological outcomes. It is not a cure, and long-term multidisciplinary care remains essential,” he said. Myelomeningocele is an open neural tube defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the spine. Children affected by the condition can develop paralysis, hydrocephalus and other lifelong neurological disabilities. International evidence supports prenatal repair in carefully selected cases. The Management of Myelomeningocele (MOMS) trial found that 40 per cent of children who underwent prenatal repair required cerebrospinal-fluid shunt placement by 12 months, compared with 82 per cent after postnatal repair. Prenatal surgery was also associated with improved motor outcomes and reduced Chiari II hindbrain herniation. However, foetal surgery carries significant risks, including prematurity and complications related to the uterine scar, and is recommended only in specialised centres and carefully selected pregnancies. “The safety of both mother and fetus depends on detailed counselling, high-quality anaesthesia, and coordinated surveillance before and after surgery,” Sharma said. The mother and foetus will continue to undergo close multidisciplinary monitoring through the remainder of pregnancy, delivery and the newborn period, the hospital said. The procedure was provided free of cost under the government’s Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), it said. AIIMS said the mother was initially screened and counselled by the maternal-foetal medicine team, with support from radiodiagnosis and other specialists. The preoperative planning included detailed fetal imaging and operative simulation. The institute said the procedure marked the culmination of efforts to develop foetal spinal surgery capability at AIIMS. “Fourteen years ago, we spoke of the possibility of foetal spinal surgery at AIIMS. Today, that possibility has become a reality. Our next responsibility is to make it safe and accessible to the Indian families who...

articles.title: Noida police deploy 2,500 personnel across 146 sites for Chhath Puja - The News Mill
articles.content: ANI Photo | Noida police deploy 2,500 personnel across 146 sites for Chhath Puja The Gautam Buddha Nagar Police have deployed approximately 2,500 civil police personnel and two companies of the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) to ensure the peaceful and smooth celebration of Chhath Puja across the district, Additional/Joint Commissioner of Police Sankalp Sharma stated. Senior police officers have conducted physical inspections of all natural and artificial ghats where devotees are expected to offer prayers. Necessary arrangements, including lighting and security measures, have been implemented at all designated locations to facilitate devotees and maintain safety during the celebrations. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google Chhath Puja will be observed at 146 locations across Gautam Buddha Nagar, with 13 sites typically attracting larger crowds. Special arrangements have been made at these key locations for crowd management and law enforcement. For effective deployment and monitoring, Gautam Buddha Nagar has been divided into 10 zones and 26 sectors, with police personnel assigned accordingly. The overall force includes around 2,500 civil police and two PAC companies to cover the district comprehensively. ADVERTISEMENT Expressing confidence in the preparations, Sharma said, “We are confident that the Chhath festival will be conducted very successfully and carried out in a smooth and orderly manner.” Chhath Puja is a four-day Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of the Sun God, Surya, and Chhathi Maiya, symbolising purity, devotion and gratitude. This year it began with Nahay Khay on November 13, which involves devotees taking a holy bath and preparing a traditional meal of Arwa rice, chana dal, and lauki (bottle gourd). The second day, Kharna on November 14, includes a fast observed from sunrise to sunset with abstinence from food and water. The fast is broken after sunset with prayers and offerings of jaggery-based kheer and roti, followed by a rigorous 36-hour fast without food or water. ADVERTISEMENT On the third day, Sandhya Arghya, devotees gather at riverbanks and water bodies to offer prayers to the setting sun. The festival concludes on November 16 with Usha Arghya, when prayers are offered to the rising sun at dawn, followed by Parana, the conclusion of the fast. Devotees seek blessings for the health, prosperity and well-being of their families during the celebrations. Written by TNM (With ANI Inputs) This story is written by TNM Bureau with inputs from ANI. articles.title: PM Modi inaugurates India's first 8K-resolution LED Dome Planetarium 'COSMOS' in Mysuru
articles.content: PM Modi inaugurates India's first 8K-resolution LED Dome Planetarium 'COSMOS' in Mysuru By : Vartha Bharati Update: 2026-11-14 08:33 GMT COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, first LED Dome planetarium of India, in Mysuru. (PC: PTI) Mysuru: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated COSMOS, India’s first tilted 8K LED dome planetarium, at the foothills of Chamundi Hill in Mysuru on Friday. The 160-seater planetarium, built at a cost of Rs 115 crore, has been jointly developed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) and the University of Mysore. It is one-of-its-kind in the world in terms of its active pixel array and real-time data integration. Unlike conventional planetariums that use projectors, COSMOS uses individually controlled LED panels to display visuals. Its dome has 6,150 LED panels carrying 4.2 crore pixels, exceeding the standard 8K benchmark. The panels produce high-contrast images across the 15-metre curved surface. Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Modi stressed the need to give priority to scientific research, innovation and opportunities for young people. He said opening the space sector to private players had enabled companies and start-ups to develop and launch rockets and satellites. “Our satellites help fishermen, track trains' real-time, and provide data for crop insurance,” the PM said. The planetarium will also screen an in-house film exploring the links between Mysuru’s history and astronomy. Shows will be available in Kannada, English and Hindi. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman described the facility as an important addition to Mysuru's tradition of learning and scholarship. “India’s first LED dome planetarium brings many important benefits. COSMOS makes astronomy accessible through an immersive learning experience. It helps children understand stars and planets and encourages them to ask questions,” she said. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced the Karnataka government’s support for a proposed COSMOS centre at Hampi. He stressed the need to make scientific facilities available in different parts of the state. With Kannada content and student mentorship, COSMOS is expected to extend science education to rural schools. Tags: COSMOS LED dome planetarium Mysuru PM Modi Nirmala Sitharaman

articles.title: India's First Indigenous Insecticide Pioxaniliprole - GKToday
articles.content: Home India’s First Indigenous Insecticide Pioxaniliprole India’s First Indigenous Insecticide Pioxaniliprole November 14, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 PI Industries has launched Pioxaniliprole, India’s first indigenously discovered insecticide molecule, under the trade name Pioxazon. The Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee formally recognised it as the first insecticide active ingredient discovered in India at its 476th meeting. Approval, formulation and crop uses Approved as a 20% weight-by-volume Suspension Concentrate, Pioxaniliprole is registered for rice, chilli, tomato and Bengal gram (chana), and for use against fall armyworm in maize. Its target pests include yellow stem borer and leaf folder in rice; fall armyworm, fruit borer and tobacco caterpillar in chilli; fruit borer in tomato; and pod borer in Bengal gram. Commercial launches began on 31 October 2026, with a nationwide rollout from 6 November during the Rabi season. Mode of action and development Pioxaniliprole belongs to the anthranilic diamide class and acts on ryanodine receptors, disrupting calcium regulation in insect muscle cells. This causes paralysis, stops feeding and ultimately kills the insect. PI Industries developed the molecule after more than a decade of research and has invested about ₹2,000 crore in overall research and development since 2014. The company plans to generate data for markets including the United States, Mexico and Brazil. Important Facts for Exams Chemical subclass: Pioxaniliprole is an anthranilic diamide; flubendiamide and cyhalodiamide, by contrast, are phthalic diamides. Pest spectrum: Diamide insecticides act mainly against lepidopteran pests, including caterpillars, a useful class-level context for Pioxaniliprole. IRAC group: Pioxaniliprole belongs to the diamides, which IRAC places in Group 28 in its mode-of-action classification. articles.title: AIIMS Delhi Performs India's First In-Utero Spinal Surgery, Successfully Operates on 25 ...
articles.content: New Delhi, November 14 (HS): The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, has performed India’s first open fetal surgery to correct myelomeningocele, a serious congenital spinal defect, in an unborn baby. The six-hour procedure was carried out on a 25-week-old foetus to repair an opening in the lower part of the spine through which cerebrospinal fluid was leaking. According to AIIMS, the surgery was performed at its Neurosciences Centre on Thursday. More than five weeks of meticulous preparation preceded the procedure, involving detailed fetal imaging, consultations among specialists, counselling of the parents, anaesthesia planning and surgical rehearsals. More than 30 doctors and nursing professionals from the departments of obstetrics and gynaecology, maternal-fetal medicine, neurosurgery, anaesthesia, plastic surgery, radiology and neonatology participated in the procedure. Professor Deepak Gupta led the neurosurgical team, while Professor Neena Malhotra and Professor K. Aparna Sharma oversaw maternal-fetal medicine and obstetric care. The surgery was performed with the assistance of high-resolution microscopy and continuous ultrasound guidance. Myelomeningocele is the most severe form of spina bifida, a congenital condition in which the spinal cord and its protective membranes protrude through an opening in the spine. The condition can lead to paralysis, hydrocephalus (an abnormal accumulation of fluid in the brain) and lifelong neurological complications. India also faces a considerable burden of neural tube defects. A review of 27 Indian studies published in 2024 estimated their average prevalence at 9.46 cases per 1,000 births. The review also highlighted the need to strengthen nationwide surveillance and monitoring systems. Professor Deepak Gupta, president of the Indian Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery, described the procedure as an important step towards establishing new capabilities in fetal medicine and paediatric neurosurgery in India. He said that, in carefully selected cases, surgery before birth aims to protect exposed neural tissue from further damage, reduce the likelihood of requiring a shunt later to drain excess cerebrospinal fluid and improve certain neurological outcomes. However, he emphasised that the procedure is not a complete cure and that the child will require long-term multidisciplinary medical care. Professor Neena Malhotra described the achievement as the outcome of the collective commitment and coordinated efforts of specialists from multiple disciplines. Professor Aparna Sharma said that decisions involving such complex fetal procedures are taken only after detailed planning, with the health and safety of both the mother and the unborn child as the primary considerations. She stressed that appropriate counselling, advanced anaesthesia management and coordinated monitoring before and after surgery are essential to ensuring maternal and fetal safety. International Research Highlights Benefits and Risks of Fetal Surgery Fetal surgery for myelomeningocele has also been extensively studied internationally. According to the Management of Myelomeningocele Study (MOMS), the proportion of children requiring a shunt to drain cerebrospinal fluid by the age of 12 months was 40 per cent among those who underwent prenatal surgery, compared with 82 per cent among children who underwent surgery after birth. articles.title: Southern India's First Barrier Free Toll Plazas Are Now Live! - Cartoq
articles.content: Southern India's First Barrier Free Toll Plazas Are Now Live [Video] Written By: Neeraj Padmakumar Published: November 14, 2026 at 12:55 PM Updated: November 14, 2026 at 12:55 PM The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is rolling out the barrier-free tolling system in more parts of the country in a phased manner. The authority has now set up the first Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling systems in southern India, and interestingly, they are both in Tamil Nadu. The first is the Paranur toll plaza and the second is the Nemili plaza. The MLFF system allows vehicles to pass through without having to stop to pay the toll. This system works based on cameras and FASTag technology. Paranur Toll Plaza Was The First NHAI introduced the MLFF system at the Paranur Toll Plaza on October 1, 2026. Located near Chengalpattu on the 46.5-km Tambaram-Tindivanam section of National Highway 45. It became Tamil Nadu's first toll plaza to adopt the fully-automated toll collection system. Vehicles travelling along this stretch no longer had top stop at the plaza to make payments. Overhead equipment reads the vehicle's FASTag and captures its registration number as it passes through the tolling zone. Payment is processed automatically based on this data. India’s first MLFF tolling setup was introduced on the Kamrej-Choryasi section between Surat and Bharuch in Gujarat in May 2026. Paranur’s installation followed this. NHAI is working on introducing barrier-free tolling on more roads in parts of Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan. Nemili Toll Plaza Gets Barrier-Free Tolling Tamil Nadu’s second and NHAI’s latest installation of the MLFF system is at the Nemili plaza. It is on the Sriperumbudur-Karaipettai section of National Highway 48. It was taken operational on November 13, 2026. Here too, the system uses advanced electronic equipment and technologies to identify vehicles and charge toll as they pass through the tolling zone. A press release put out by PIB Chennai claims that the MLFF system can effectively curtail traffic congestion by minimising the need for human intervention. This can, in the larger picture, reduce travel time, fuel consumption and emissions. It also claims that operational efficiencies are further heightened through optimized lane throughput and reduced physical infrastructure overheads. The authority has advised motorists to keep their FASTags valid and ensure they have sufficient balance in them. Vehicles with insufficient balance or an invalid or non-functional FASTag may receive e-notices. What Is The MLFF Tolling System And How Does It Work? Multi-Lane Free Flow is a barrier-free toll collection technology that allows vehicles to pass through tolling points without stopping or entering a dedicated toll lane. It uses a combination of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), FASTag-based Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) and other vehicle-detection technologies. As a vehicle approaches the tolling zone, overhead cameras capture its registration number while the FASTag system reads the tag using radio-frequency identification (RFID). The information is then used to identify the vehicle and process the applicable toll charge automatically. Some advanced MLFF installations also use LiDAR technology. Short...

articles.title: PM Modi Opens India's First LED Dome Planetarium - UdaipurTimes.com
articles.content: PM Modi Opens India's First LED Dome Planetarium COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, in Mysuru, is India's first LED dome planetarium By Razia Sanwari | Nov 14, 2026, 12:17 IST Join for live updates on WhatsApp UdaipurTimes, Nov 14, 2026 - Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday, November 13, inaugurated the country's first LED dome planetarium - the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium - in Mysuru, Karnataka. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister expressed his delight at returning to Mysuru to dedicate the COSMOS Planetarium to the Nation just months after inaugurating the Viveka Smaraka. He pointed out that while the Viveka Smaraka inspires introspection and spiritual pursuit, the COSMOS Planetarium directs the gaze skyward to unravel the mysteries of the vast universe and he emphasised the profound cultural message conveyed by both landmarks. “This is an example of the fact that in India, the traditions of spirituality and science have always moved forward together,” the Prime Minister said. Highlighting Mysuru's rich tradition of fostering knowledge institutions, including the establishment of the University of Mysore under Maharaja Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar and the Wadiyar Royal Family's pivotal role in laying the foundation of the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru to empower generations of scholars, the Prime Minister noted that Mysuru is adding a new chapter to India's scientific journey with the dedication of this state-of-the-art planetarium to the youth and citizens. PM Modi highlighted the government's decision to open the space sector to private participation, which has enabled Indian startups and youth to showcase their capabilities by launching private rockets, placing satellites into orbit and undertaking unprecedented space ventures. Stating that advancing research requires giving students and scholars access to the world's finest scientific literature, the Prime Minister mentioned the launch of One Nation One Subscription to help domestic institutes access leading global journals alongside the creation of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation. The Prime Minister concluded his address by urging those associated with COSMOS to continuously invite school and college students from across the region and extended his best wishes for the journey ahead. “The children who come here to learn about the universe, it is possible that some of them may return here one day and tell us what new discoveries they have made about the universe, and this alone will be the biggest success of this COSMOS Planetarium,” PM Modi said. articles.title: PM Modi hails COSMOS, calls it extraordinary experience - The New Indian Express
articles.content: MYSURU: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said the state-of-the-art COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium would inspire young minds to explore the mysteries of the universe and contribute to India’s growing scientific achievements. Speaking after dedicating COSMOS-Mysuru, India’s first LED Dome Planetarium, to the nation, Modi said the facility would add a new chapter to India’s scientific journey and provide students and researchers with opportunities to develop scientific curiosity and pursue new discoveries. Drawing a parallel between the Viveka Smaraka, which he had inaugurated in Mysuru recently, and COSMOS-Mysuru, Modi said the two institutions conveyed a profound message about India’s traditions of spirituality and science. While Viveka Smaraka inspired people to look within and seek spiritual knowledge, COSMOS encouraged them to look towards the skies and understand the vast universe. “India’s traditions of spirituality and science have always progressed together,” he said, recalling the contributions of ancient Indian astronomers Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Neelakantha Somayaji, who made significant discoveries and complex calculations without modern instruments and technology. Speaking of Mysuru’s legacy of promoting education and research, he recalled that the University of Mysore was established during the reign of Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar and the Wadiyar family played an important role in laying the foundation for the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru. Congratulating the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, University of Mysore, government departments and those associated with the project, Modi described COSMOS as an extraordinary experience. Referring to India’s achievements in international science competitions, he said five Indian students participated in the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics in Vietnam this year, four won gold medals and one got silver. “When young people are provided with opportunities, resources, technology, tools and institutional support, they achieve remarkable milestones,” Modi said. Highlighting India’s progress in space exploration over the past decade, Modi cited the successful Chandrayaan-3 mission and Aditya-L1 solar observatory. He said the opening up of the space sector had created new opportunities for private companies and startups, enabling young entrepreneurs to develop rockets, launch satellites and undertake activities previously unprecedented in India. Similarly, real-time train tracking systems developed by Railways and ISRO enabled passengers to check train locations and arrival times. Satellite data was also being used to estimate crop yields and determine insurance claims, he said. “Science for Society is our approach. Satellites are reaching new heights in space, and improving the lives of people on Earth,” he added. Referring to the `1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation scheme launched last year, Modi said it would ensure adequate funding for researchers and help translate new technologies into practical applications. He called for greater participation of school and college students at COSMOS. “Some of the children who visit COSMOS today may return one day with new discoveries about the universe.
